messages.subject: Areal models
parts:
I have the areal model(spatio-temporal) shown below. 

formulaf<-y ~ 1 + f(region.struct1,model="besag",graph="KEN.adj",hyper = list(prec = list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.001))))+
                    f(region.unstruct1,model="iid")+
                    f(time.struct1,model="rw1", hyper = list(prec = list(prior="pc.prec",param=c(0.33,0.01))))+
                    f(time.unstruct1,model="iid")+
                    f(ID.Region.Year,model="iid")
modf<-inla(formulaf,family="binomial",data=data,Ntrials=pop,
           control.inla=list(diagonal=1e-4),
           control.predictor=list(compute=T,link=1),
           control.compute = list(dic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE),verbose=TRUE)



The data are at 47 geographical units and spans across 30 years. In some cases I have an year with two or more  raw estimates. When I run the model, I expected the model to return one single mean. Bt that not the case. for unit 15 in the year 2000, why is that the smoothed estimates are different.Yet its the same year
Year geo_Unit Raw smoothed
2000 15 20 20.64599
2000 15 48.81801 47.4542

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Areal models
parts:
you will, with two observations for one linear predictor, have two
linear predictors that is the same, and each one is the same as if you
had two observations.

this simple example shows it and compares with the MLE estimate


> n = 100

> lambda = 10

> y = rpois(n, lambda = lambda)

> x = rnorm(n, sd = 0.1)

> formula = y ~ 1

> r = inla(formula, data = data.frame(y, x), family = "poisson",
+ control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE))

> ## new additional data
> yy = rpois(n, lambda = lambda)

> rr = inla(formula, data = data.frame(y = c(y, yy)),
+ family = "poisson",
+ control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE))

> cbind(r$summary.fitted.values[10, "sd"], sqrt(mean(y)/n))
[,1] [,2]
[1,] 0.3246564825 0.3234192326

> cbind(rr$summary.fitted.values[10, "sd"], sqrt(mean(c(y,yy))/n/2))
[,1] [,2]
[1,] 0.2274320228 0.22588714

>
